newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end 1.08 pct higher on heavyweights.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end 1.08 pct higher on heavyweights.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended 1.08 percent higher on heavyweight buying on Thursday ahead of Eid al-Fitr Moslem celebrations starting on Friday, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 7.42 points, or 1.08 percent, to close at 694.28 points after falling to 685.74 points in early trade. The market is closed from Friday to next Wednesday.
In broader market sentiment, gainers led losers by 69 to 35, with 73 counters unchanged.
"The underlying tone is very, very strong. It may go up after the market re-opens next Wednesday," a foreign broker with a European securities house said.
Many brokers were surprised at the sustained buying interest led by local investors in heavyweights as they usually took sell positions ahead of the holiday.
"I would have thought there would be some selling from the local players, but they are not doing that," the foreign broker said.
"This is a pretty good news. There is a lot of strength in the market," he added.
Brokers said a further rise in blue chip telecommunications firm Indosat on the perception that its 1996 earnings were slightly better than expected also boosted overall market sentiment.
Heavyweight Bank Negara Indonesia was the most active stock with 16.5 million shares traded. It closed 50 rupiah higher at 1,650 rupiah on what brokers said was fresh-buying on its fundamentals.
The stock with the heaviest weight on the index, telecommunications firm Telkom, rose 50 rupiah to 4,200 rupiah on a volume of 1.4 million shares.
Fisheries firm Daya Guna Samudera was second on the active list, with buying boosted by media reports that it had got government approval to import fishing vessels this year.
It rose 150 rupiah to 3,800 rupiah on 4.4 million shares.
